claims.text: Fried items — squid tempura, fugu fry, oyster fry, wagyu katsu — are all listed on the menu, making shared fryer cross-contamination a realistic concern. No dedicated fryer information is disclosed.
Wheat-based soy sauce is standard in kappo cuisine and is expected in grilled (yakimono) and simmered dishes. No tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned.
Fish dashi (likely bonito/katsuo or kombu-bonito blend) is standard in Japanese kappo; no plant-based dashi option is mentioned. Virtually all dishes will contain animal products.
No allergy policy or staff allergy-handling procedures are published. The chef is known to accommodate special requests when informed in advance — contact by phone (079-288-1302) before visiting.
No information is available about fryer sharing between different menu items (chicken, croquettes, fried takoyaki). Cross-contamination risk cannot be ruled out.

The karaage marinade almost certainly uses conventional Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat. The batter is standard wheat-flour coating. Neither the shop nor any third-party source has published allergen or ingredient details.
The entire menu is meat-based; there is no plant-based cooking context here and cross-contact is not a relevant concern given no vegan items exist.
No information on staff allergy awareness or handling procedures is available from any source reviewed. Direct contact is required: 080-9014-9354.
Tempura is a core menu item (anago tempura, vegetable tempura) cooked in shared kitchen oil using wheat-flour batter. No dedicated fryer or allergen separation is documented.
Braised anago (conger eel) dishes rely on conventional Japanese soy sauce (shoyu), which contains wheat. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternative is mentioned anywhere.
Dashi stock (likely katsuobushi/bonito-based) is standard in miso soup, noodle broths, and simmered preparations throughout the menu. No plant-based dashi option is mentioned.
No allergen menu, allergy chart, or documented staff allergy-handling procedure appears on the official site or in any guest review. The restaurant does not list dietary accommodations as a feature.
Non-smoking throughout; Himeji-area Wi-Fi available; credit cards and QR code payments accepted, reducing cash-handling stress for visitors.
セルフ式でお客が具材をトレーに盛るスタイルのため、小麦含有食品（小麦麺・揚げパンなど）との交差汚染リスクが考えられる。専用グルテンフリー調理環境の情報なし。
中国式の麻辣湯スープには醤油・豆板醤等の調味料が使用される可能性が高く、これらには通常小麦が含まれる。スープの具体的な原材料リストは公開されていない。
ベーススープは牛骨出汁であるため、同じ鍋・調理器具で野菜具材を調理する場合、ビーガン非対応となる。
アレルギー対応・グルテンフリー対応に関する公式情報は一切公開されていない。来店前に電話（080-5301-5588）またはX（@umaimaratan）で確認することを強く推奨する。
約60種類の具材から自分で選べるセルフスタイルのため、野菜・きのこ類のみを選択することはできる。辛さは5段階から調整可能。
No information on cross-contamination controls. This is a small open counter grill; shared cooking surfaces are standard for yakitori-ya and no GF protocol has been documented anywhere.

Yakitori tare (the standard glaze applied to grilled skewers) is soy-sauce-based and contains wheat. The signature ひねぽん uses ponzu, which in Japan typically also contains soy sauce. Wheat exposure is likely on most non-shio (salt-only) items.
Every dish involves chicken or chicken-derived ingredients (offal stew, tori-sashi, yakitori). Any vegetable side dish shares prep space with raw chicken.

No allergy-handling protocol documented in any source. One reviewer noted a custom shio-only request was casually accommodated, suggesting flexibility, but this is not evidence of allergen-safe preparation.
Salt-grilled (shio) skewers are available on request and can be prepared without tare glaze, potentially reducing (but not eliminating) soy sauce exposure for those with mild sensitivity.

name: 杵屋 姫路山陽百貨店 (Kineya Himeji Sanyo Department Store)

claims.text: Gourmet Kineya's corporate allergen documentation states that cross-contamination of allergens during cooking cannot be completely prevented across all menu items.
Standard soy sauce containing wheat is used in the broth and dipping sauces. All udon noodles are made in-house from wheat flour. No wheat-free soy sauce alternative is offered.
All broth is made with katsuobushi (bonito flakes) and kombu dashi — no plant-based broth option is listed. Tempura items are fried in shared oil with shrimp tempura on the menu.

The company publishes a per-item allergen PDF covering the 8 mandatory Japanese allergens (wheat, buckwheat, egg, dairy, peanut, shrimp, crab, walnut), but explicitly notes that full prevention of cross-contamination cannot be guaranteed.
Gourmet Kineya publishes a downloadable allergen chart for all menu items on their corporate website, making it possible to check each dish before ordering.
グルテン交差汚染に関する情報は一切公開されていない。刺身中心の業態だが、厨房での小麦使用状況は不明。
醤油ベースの調理が複数メニューに使われており（水ナスしそしょうが正油など）、通常の小麦入り醤油が使用されていると考えられる。
鰹節・魚介だしを使用した伝統的な日本料理店。植物性への配慮・切り替えに関する記録はなし。
アレルギー対応・グルテンフリー対応についての記載は食べログ・ヒトサラ・エキテンいずれにも見当たらない。訪問前に電話（079-223-1129）で直接確認を推奨。
刺身そのものは基本的に無添加・小麦不使用で提供されることが多く、醤油を避ければ選べる品がある可能性はある。

name: 喫茶 フクナガ (Kissa Fukunaga)

claims.text: No allergen or soy sauce information published. The curry, pasta, and egg sandwich are all likely to involve wheat-based soy sauce or wheat-containing ingredients; no source confirms tamari or GF substitutes are available.
Dairy and eggs are core ingredients across the menu (Italian pudding, canelé, egg sandwich, cream sodas). No vegan cross-contact protocols documented.
